page: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-2xL40S is an accelerated compute server instance configured with 32 shared vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz on x86_64 architecture. Memory allocation stands at 384.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a high density of 12.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by two NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPUs delivering a cumulative 96 GB of VRAM. Virtualization is driven by KVM, complemented by vector extension instruction support including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. The instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions, and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate top-tier execution across general compute and parallel processing. Geekbench results record a single-core score of 2,736.0 and a multi-core score of 25,199.0, both placing in the top 10 percent. Multi-core stress-ng tests achieve 131,937.77, while PassMark CPU benchmarks register 87,135.2. Memory subsystem throughput shows 327.05 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 126.98 GB/sec on large-block writes, complemented by high-performance data processing evidenced by Redis SET operations reaching 127.0 million ops/sec.

GPU acceleration enables strong throughput on small-to-medium parameter machine learning workloads. For small models (135M), LLM inference prompt processing reaches 5,508.2 tokens per second with text generation at 360.16 tokens per second. Performance on 7B parameter models remains strong at 220.88 tokens per second prompt processing and 38.13 tokens per second generation. However, when executing 70B parameter models, throughput declines into middle-tier averages, reaching 21.91 tokens per second prompt ingestion and 4.14 tokens per second generation.

Qualitatively, the server provides substantial compute, memory, and accelerator density in a single virtual machine without requiring full dedicated chassis allocations. The lack of integrated local NVMe storage represents a key tradeoff, shifting disk I/O performance entirely to attached network block volumes. UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-2xL40S is suited for deep learning inference on models up to medium sizes, image and text processing pipelines, distributed database operations, and high-concurrency analytical microservices.

Equipped with dual NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPUs providing 96 GB of total VRAM, the instance targets parallel processing and AI inference workloads. Benchmark evaluations show top 10% compute capabilities, marked by a multi-core Geekbench score of 25,199.0 and 127.0 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware vector capabilities feature AVX-512 and BF16, while LLM benchmarks demonstrate high performance on small and medium models, alongside reduced generation speeds on 70B parameter configurations. The platform includes no bundled local storage, relying on external network storage. This server fits workloads such as real-time machine learning inference, multimedia processing, large in-memory databases, and high-throughput scientific simulation pipelines.
